what: Starting rules that turn the Assess parts (growth model output, NASA alarm times, the fuel and the verdict) into a level: Low, Elevated or High. A team choice, to be approved. The rules are read in file order and the first rule whose test holds fires (js/assess_core.js riskLevel). Every rule compares two computed values, or checks a category; none uses a fixed threshold number. The detection shares from whatif.json and drift_whatif.json are shown as parts but no rule uses them, because they do not change with the visitor's inputs.
test_grammar: test is a list of conditions that must all hold. Each condition is {a, op, b} (compare value a with value b) or {a, op, value} (compare value a with a fixed category value). op is one of == != > >= < <=. a and b name entries in 'values'. If a value a rule needs is missing, that rule cannot be checked; the chain stops there and the default level fires, saying which value was missing.

values.kind: what the growth model did with the input: growth, droplet, unsupported or invalid
values.verdict_code: M6b verdict from NASA's observed cases: 0 spreads, 1 near observed extinction, 2 observed no-spread (data/spread_predictor.json verdict_codes)
values.frame_time_s: time of the flame reading, s after ignition
values.initial_area_cm2: starting flame area on the model grid, cm2
values.max_area_lo_cm2: largest burning area in the lo run, cm2
values.max_area_mid_cm2: largest burning area in the mid run, cm2
values.max_area_hi_cm2: largest burning area in the hi run, cm2
values.t_max_mid_abs_s: time of the largest burning area in the mid run, s after ignition (frame time + time to max)
values.t_max_hi_abs_s: time of the largest burning area in the hi run, s after ignition (frame time + time to max)
values.t_end_hi_abs_s: time the hi-run fire ends, s after ignition
values.stop_reason_hi: why the hi run stopped: fuel edge, burned out, or observed no-spread conditions
values.out_of_box: how many inputs lie outside the calibration box of the active regime
values.radiometer_s: slowest flame-radiometer alarm over the Saffire-III burns with a radiometer alarm, s after ignition (data/saffire_latency.json)
values.smoke_fastest_s: fastest cabin smoke-detector (scatter) alarm over those burns, s after ignition (data/saffire_latency.json)
values.smoke_slowest_s: slowest cabin smoke-detector (scatter) alarm over those burns, s after ignition (data/saffire_latency.json)
values.cabin_caught_120: share of simulated cabin fires caught within 120 s by the named whatif.json layout (shown, not used by a rule)
values.lbm_caught_180: share of simulated fires caught within 180 s by the best drift_whatif.json layout (shown, not used by a rule)

rules.label: No growth run
rules.reason: The growth model ran no simulation for this input (a droplet flame, a material it does not model, or an input it cannot use), so no level is given. A droplet flame is covered by the M7 extinction and burning-rate models on Put it out.

rules.label: Still growing at the slowest smoke alarm
rules.reason: In the hi run the burning area is still growing at the time of the slowest cabin smoke-detector alarm, so the crew could first hear of this fire while it is still getting bigger. The alarm times are seconds after ignition on NASA's Saffire-III orbital burns, a different fire, shown for scale only and not as a prediction for this one.

rules.label: Spreads, peaks before the slowest smoke alarm
rules.reason: NASA's observed cases do not rule out spread here and the hi run grows beyond the starting flame, but it reaches its largest size before the slowest cabin smoke-detector alarm. The alarm times are seconds after ignition on NASA's Saffire-III orbital burns, a different fire, shown for scale only and not as a prediction for this one.

rules.label: Near observed extinction, still grows
rules.reason: The conditions are close to a NASA case where the flame went out, but the hi run still grows beyond the starting flame. A small change in airflow or oxygen could go either way.

rules.label: NASA observed no spread here
rules.reason: A matched NASA case recorded no spread at these conditions, so the model holds the flame at its starting size until it burns out. Check the matched cases: some are 'reported', not checked by us. Low is not a statement that the fire is harmless.

rules.label: Does not grow
rules.reason: Even the hi run never grows beyond the starting flame. Low is not a statement that the fire is harmless.

default.label: No rule matched
default.reason: No rule matched, so the team default applies. The default is Elevated, not Low, so an unmatched case is never shown as reassuring.
